record.paper_title: Open problems on countable dense homogeneity
record.original_question: Does there exist a Bernstein subset of the real line that is countable dense homogeneous, where a Bernstein subset of R is one whose set and complement both meet every Cantor set in R?

evidence.quote: A subset X of R is called Bernstein if X and R \ X intersect every Cantor set in R.
Problem 13 (Baldwin and Beaudoin [7]). Is there a Bernstein subset of R which is CDH?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A subset X of the real line ℝ is called a Bernstein set if both X and its complement ℝ ∖ X intersect every Cantor set in ℝ (where a Cantor set means a subset of ℝ homeomorphic to the standard Cantor middle-thirds set). A topological space Y is called countable dense homogeneous (CDH) if for any two countable dense subsets A, B of Y there is a homeomorphism h: Y → Y with h(A) = B.

Decide, in ZFC, whether there exists a Bernstein subset of ℝ (equipped with the subspace topology inherited from ℝ) that is countable dense homogeneous.
artifact.status_search_result: Baldwin and Beaudoin (1989) showed that under Martin's axiom MA(σ-centered) there exists a CDH Bernstein subset of the reals (or equivalently of 2^ω). However, no ZFC construction (nor a consistency result for nonexistence) appears to be known, and the question is still listed among open problems on countable dense homogeneity.

status_evidence.title: Countable dense homogeneous spaces under Martin's axiom
status_evidence.snippet: Baldwin and Beaudoin (Israel J. Math., 1989) construct a CDH Bernstein set under MA.
status_evidence.claim: Existence of a CDH Bernstein subset of ℝ is known consistent under Martin's axiom.

status_evidence.title: Countable dense homogeneity and set theory (Medini)
status_evidence.snippet: Under MA(σ-centered), there is a CDH Bernstein X ⊆ 2^ω.
status_evidence.claim: Bernstein CDH sets exist consistently; no ZFC resolution mentioned.

status_evidence.title: Open problems on countable dense homogeneity
status_evidence.snippet: List of open problems including whether a Bernstein CDH subset of R exists.
status_evidence.claim: The question is listed as an open problem.
